findings.title: Anyone signed in with an invite link can take the invited teammate's access — acceptance never checks the invited email or consumes the token
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a signed-in recipient of a forwarded or leaked invite link can bind it to a different email, read the team's system and files, and, for an Editor invite, overwrite work. Reusing the link reassigns user_id again, potentially displacing the intended teammate. No owner approval is required; owner removal of the member is the available recovery.
findings.evidence: backend/projects.py:226 looks up only members.invite_token; :229-230 sets members.$.user_id to the caller without comparing members.email or marking the invite used. role_for at :33-35 grants the bound user that member's role. frontend/src/pages/AuthPages.jsx:72-75 automatically accepts the token.
findings.expected: R-076: "is refused when the caller's email differs from the invited address" and "only once"; request: "An invite is sent to an email address." Acceptance must bind only that address and must not let another account replay it.
reproduction_steps: As owner, invite teammate A as Editor and copy the invite link.
Sign in with a different email B and open that link.
The code accepts B and opens the project with Editor access.
Open the same link as another signed-in account; the membership is rebound again.

findings.title: Two editors can silently overwrite each other's saves — version check is separate from the unconditional update
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that two editors saving from version 1 concurrently can both pass the read-time check before either update. Both writes then succeed (versions 2 and 3), with the latter replacing the former system and inputs, and neither editor receives an overwrite warning. Consequential generated team work is lost without history (Phase 2 is not implemented).
findings.evidence: backend/projects.py:163-168 reads and compares the version, then :169-172 find_one_and_update filters only project_id and increments version. frontend/src/pages/Workspace.jsx:273 sends base_version and :281 shows the warning only on 409.
findings.expected: R-068: "you are warned before overwriting"; R-069: an older base_version "returns 409 ... and writes nothing"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "conditional/atomic operations" must protect concurrent commit points. Exactly one version-1 save may commit without a warning.
reproduction_steps: Owner and Editor open the same version of a project.
Make different changes in each workspace.
Press Save in both while the requests overlap so both load the old version before either update.
Both return success; reopen and observe that only the later system remains, without a conflict dialog.

findings.title: Removed teammates can still fetch their uploaded project files — uploader bypass skips current project permissions
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a removed Editor retains authenticated download access to every project file they uploaded even after membership removal or project deletion, and retains delete/use-in-generation access to their references after demotion to Viewer. This defeats the team's revocation boundary; the owner cannot revoke this file access through Share or project deletion.
findings.evidence: backend/projects.py:311-312 returns any file directly to its uploader for a viewer/read check, before :314 load_project. For reference files it also returns directly for editor/delete checks. :187-189 deleting a project only marks the project deleted and never marks files deleted. :341-349 loads references using this same bypass.
findings.expected: Request: "Members can upload, download and delete files, according to their role"; R-065: deletion "removes the project and its files"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Follow ... membership removal ... through every supported access path." Project-linked files must always enforce the current project role and live-project state.
reproduction_steps: As Editor upload a project file and attach a reference; retain their file ids.
As owner remove this Editor in Share (or delete the project).
As the former Editor request download of the uploaded file by its existing file id.
The uploader shortcut still serves it; a reference can also still be deleted or used in generation.

findings.title: Opening another project during synthesis can save the first project's output over it — late completion is not tied to its project
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a user generating A can open B during the 40–90 second job; A's delayed result then replaces B's displayed system while B's name, role and version stay selected. Pressing Save writes A's code and inputs over B without a conflict because B's version is current. There is no version history to recover B's overwritten system. The running task needs an operation/project identity guard or navigation protection.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:187 awaits generation then :188-191 unconditionally replaces result using the original closure. :305-311 can independently replace project and result while the await runs. ProjectsPanel.jsx:90 open buttons remain enabled while busy (only Stack at :76 uses busy). Workspace.jsx:273 subsequently saves the displayed result to the currently selected project's id.
findings.expected: Request: projects hold their own "latest generated system" and inputs; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "including late completion after cancel" and context restoration must preserve valid work.
reproduction_steps: Open A and start a regeneration.
Before it finishes, click B's Open row in Projects.
Wait for A's generation to finish; the header still names B but result/context come from A.
Press Save, then reopen B; its previous output has been replaced by A's generation.

findings.title: A pre-registered password retains access to the real Google user's projects — account linking trusts an unverified existing email
findings.surface: Email registration → Google account linking → email sign-in
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts someone who pre-registers a teammate's email can keep their chosen password after the real teammate signs in with Google. The real teammate sees a successful Google session and creates private projects in the same user_id; the earlier registrant can log in by password to read or modify those projects and files. No victim password or Google credentials are required for the pre-registration. The victim would need owner-assisted reset to regain sole access.
findings.evidence: auth.py:127-134 permits registering an unverified email with a password. :168-171 merges a subsequent Google sign-in into that row and sets email_verified True, without removing or re-proving its existing password. :147-156 continues accepting that password. Project ownership is keyed by user_id (projects.py:31).
findings.expected: R-055: "same email address ... one account" must preserve secure identity; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Establish the actual principals and trust model" and "OAuth ... link/create once". Linking a provider-verified email must not leave an unrelated unverified registrant with ongoing access.
reproduction_steps: Register an email/password account using another person's email (without email verification).
Have the actual email owner sign in through Google with that address and save a private project.
Sign in with the password chosen during pre-registration.
That session has the same user_id and can access the real owner's newly saved work.

findings.title: Signing out does not revoke email sessions — access and refresh JWTs have no server-side session or revocation check
findings.surface: Sign out; POST /api/auth/logout and /refresh; authenticated APIs
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a retained email access token can continue reading and writing private projects for its remaining 15 minutes after Sign out; a retained refresh credential can mint further access for seven days. Clearing the UI cookies does not invalidate a captured session. Signing out therefore cannot terminate a compromised/shared email session; Google sessions do have a database deletion path.
findings.evidence: auth.py:32 JWT payload has sub/type/exp but no session identity; :55-62 validates signature and user existence only. Logout :207-210 deletes only Google session rows and client cookies. Refresh :196-201 accepts the previous signed refresh token without a revoked-session lookup.
findings.expected: Request: "sign-out"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "next-request rejection of revoked/deleted sessions" and "Sign-out ... ends a server-held session." A signed-out email session must not remain usable with its old credentials.
reproduction_steps: Sign in with email/password and retain that session's credentials in an authorized API client.
Use Account menu → Sign out.
Reuse the old access credential for GET /api/projects; it remains accepted until expiry.
Reuse the old refresh credential for POST /api/auth/refresh; it can still renew access.

findings.title: Unsolicited Google callbacks can log a visitor into another account — callback exchange lacks browser-bound state validation
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts an unsolicited callback URL containing a valid broker session identifier for a different account is exchanged and sets that account's session cookie, without proof that this browser initiated that login. A signed-out visitor can be logged into another person's account and unknowingly save private UE5 work there. Broker-side validity proves the identifier's identity, not this browser's intent; actual broker issuance behavior was not executed.
findings.evidence: Login.jsx:35-38 starts broker auth with redirect only, with no app nonce. App.js:21 accepts any session_id fragment. AuthPages.jsx:18-19 exchanges it immediately. auth.py:161-163 receives only session_id and verifies it with the provider but never binds it to a browser-initiated state.
findings.expected: R-054: "checks the OAuth state value issued at sign-in start ... a callback whose state value does not match is refused"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "validate issued state." An uninitiated callback must not change the browser's signed-in identity.
reproduction_steps: Obtain a valid broker callback identifier for account A in a controlled authentication flow.
In a different signed-out browser that never started Google login, open the app callback location carrying that identifier.
The frontend posts it and the backend sets account A's cookie without checking browser-bound state.
Saving work would then store it under A.

findings.title: Regeneration and stacking cannot preserve existing implementation — both discard source, pseudocode, graph and most code before calling Claude
findings.surface: Regenerate and Stack Systems model context
findings.observed: AI and model features: source proves custom behavior contained only in the previous .cpp, pseudocode, setup, graph or the omitted header tail is never sent on regeneration or stacking. For example, a saved damage system with a bespoke combo-reset rule only in its .cpp cannot have that rule preserved from the provided context when the user only changes Max Health, nor can stacking inspect its implementation conflicts. The model receives a summary, not the previous output. Output quality itself was not sampled; omitted context is deterministic and forces users to re-supply implementation manually.
findings.evidence: changes.js:75-83 compactForApi sends only name/summary/modules/params/network notes and the first 2500 header characters; it drops cpp_source, pseudocode, graph and setup. Workspace.jsx:220 and :238 use it for regeneration and stacking. server.py:211-222 compacts again and :236 limits stacked headers to 1800 characters. :185-186 promises preserving unaffected content and integrating systems.
findings.expected: R-087: previous output is sent with explicit revision instructions; request: "regeneration should visibly respect the edits" and stack should "combine them into a single synthesized output ... avoids conflicts." Unchanged implementation and cross-system logic must be available to the model for a faithful revision/merge.
reproduction_steps: Open a saved system whose .cpp contains an implementation detail not in its header or summary.
Change only a parameter and Synthesize, or select it with another project and Stack.
Trace compactForApi and build_user_text: the complete source, pseudocode and graph are absent from the model input.
The model cannot faithfully revise/merge that omitted implementation.

findings.title: Phone users cannot reach generated output and tuning actions — desktop-only fixed panels exceed a viewport with hidden overflow
findings.surface: Workspace and public share view at 375px width
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts that at 375px the two fixed sidebars alone require 660px, exceeding the viewport by 285px before any center content. The right dials and generated output are clipped with no outer scrolling, and full-text public header/tab buttons overflow as well. A phone user cannot complete tuning/viewing/copying through the intended workspace. This is a source layout deduction, not a browser measurement.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:426 fixes left sidebar to w-[320px] shrink-0 and :606 fixes right sidebar to w-[340px] shrink-0 in a single flex row (:423), with main min-w-0 (:502). The header (:385-419) has unwrapped branding/actions. PublicView.jsx:35-51 also uses unwrapped full-text header/tab actions. index.css:57-59 and App.css:1 hide outer overflow; there is no responsive sidebar alternative.
findings.expected: R-117: primary content and Synthesize/Copy JSON are usable "at 1440px and at 375px wide"; checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "containment ... scrolling and reachable controls under supported viewports." At narrow widths core output and actions must remain accessible.
reproduction_steps: Open the signed-in workspace at 375px CSS width.
Generate a system and try to view the central tabs and tune the right panel.
Open a public share link at the same width and try its Copy JSON and tab actions.
Fixed rows exceed the clipped viewport with no responsive navigation.

findings.title: Email/password invitees do not see invited projects on sign-in — automatic access is limited to Google-verified accounts
findings.surface: Projects → Shared with me; email sign-in
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts an invited email/password user signs in successfully but Shared with me stays empty, including when the owner invited an already registered email account. They must obtain and follow the separate invite link to gain access, defeating the promised automatic discovery. Google sign-in is the only path that sets verification (:170).
findings.evidence: backend/auth.py:132 creates email accounts with email_verified False and :140-157 login never verifies them. backend/projects.py:34 grants an unclaimed email membership only if email_verified; :114-116 adds email matches to the shared query only for verified accounts.
findings.expected: R-077 and request: "The person sees the project under 'Shared with me' as soon as they sign in with that email." Both supported sign-in methods must reach this outcome while maintaining secure email identity.
reproduction_steps: Create an email/password teammate account.
As owner add that email as Viewer or Editor in Share.
Sign in as that teammate without opening the invite link.
Open Shared with me: the query excludes the pending membership.

findings.title: Reopened projects use another project's bias and omit saved notes — openSystem never restores these inputs
findings.surface: Projects → open; Project Context and Notes for next synthesis
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts opening project A saved with 'GAS with hard attribute ceiling' while the browser context is 'realistic large-scale FPS' leaves the FPS bias displayed and used in A's next regeneration. Notes that produced A are not restored to the notes control either. Saved context exists in Mongo but is ignored, so teammates and cross-device users must reconstruct it manually and can generate the wrong architecture.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:189 stores project_context and notes in result.context; :154 initializes projectContext from browser storage; :288-298 restores dials/prompt/references but never calls setProjectContext(c.project_context); :301 unconditionally setNotes(""). :187 injects the current global projectContext into every run.
findings.expected: R-062: reopening "restores those inputs and that system"; request: a project holds "description, dials, Project Context, modules and notes" and teammates regenerate together. Opening a cloud project must restore its own bias and notes rather than an unrelated browser default.
reproduction_steps: Generate and save A with one Project Context preset and designer notes.
Change the browser's context to a different preset while working on B.
Open A from Projects.
A's saved context and notes are not restored; Synthesize sends the other preset.

findings.title: Attaching or removing references on a saved project is lost on Save — persistence uses the last synthesis's stale reference list
findings.surface: Attach reference / remove chip → Save → reopen
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts an Editor attaching a file after synthesis then saving sees the chip disappear on reopening. Conversely removing a reference and saving restores the removed chip on reopening, and a later regeneration sends that reference again. Uploading the object with a project id does not fix the issue because project reopening never discovers attached references from the file collection. Regenerating before Save is a costly, undisclosed workaround.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:156 maintains references separately; :189 copies them into result.context only when generation completes. :263-265 splitResult returns result.context unchanged; :270-274 saves that context. Files.jsx:43 and :61 update only the separate references state. openSystem at Workspace.jsx:298 restores context.references.
findings.expected: R-078: "each attached reference ... stays attached to the project for later regenerations"; request: "Each can be removed individually." Saving must persist the currently chosen reference list without requiring another paid synthesis.
reproduction_steps: Open a generated saved project.
Attach a new reference (or remove an existing reference chip).
Press Save without synthesizing again.
Reopen the project; the old reference list returns.

findings.title: Reloading or deep-linking a cloud project opens the default workspace — project identity is never retained in the URL
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts opening /projects/<id> renders an unsaved default workspace, and reloading after opening a cloud project loses the selected project and inputs. Users must find it in Projects again; browser back/forward cannot return between project selections. Saved data remains recoverable through the list.
findings.evidence: App.js:27 routes every otherwise unmatched path to Workspace without extracting a project id. Workspace.jsx:168 only reads a ?project query; :171 immediately replaces even that URL with '/'. :305-311 opens project state without changing the URL.
findings.expected: R-113: "Opening /projects/{id} directly ... loads that project's saved system ... and a reload keeps the same project open"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "direct access, reload, back and return paths" must retain the referenced object.
reproduction_steps: Open an existing project from Projects.
Reload the page: the workspace initializes with no project.
Open /projects/<that id> in a fresh signed-in tab.
The catch-all renders the default workspace without loading the id.

findings.title: Accepted reference code and PDF content is silently omitted — extraction truncates at 20,000 characters and 40 pages
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts an accepted 30 KB .h whose class declaration lies after a long license/comment prefix loses that entire declaration before generation, and a PDF's page 41 is never considered. The chip still shows a successful attachment and the full file is stored, so developers pay for a synthesis that cannot follow the omitted specification without knowing to split/rewrite it. UTF-8 text and PDF extraction do reach Claude for content inside those silent bounds.
findings.evidence: projects.py:22 sets TEXT_CHARS=20000; :261 takes PDF pages[:40] then text[:TEXT_CHARS]; :265 truncates decoded code/text to 20000 characters. :299-304 stores the full original size and reports successful attachment without a truncation flag. server.py:230-232 sends only that extracted text.
findings.expected: R-104 and request: "AI uses them as source material", e.g. "extend this existing header"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Compare complete intended content and actual input selection" and make skipped input visible. Within the stated 10 MB acceptance limit, required content must reach the model or limitations must be communicated before synthesis.
reproduction_steps: Attach a valid UTF-8 header under 10 MB with the declared class after character 20,000 (or a spec with requirements on PDF page 41).
Ask to extend that class or implement that requirement and Synthesize.
The model prompt receives only the truncated prefix.
No attachment or generation UI reports that the required content was omitted.

findings.title: Abandoned synthesis keeps polling after navigation or sign-out — async polling has no lifecycle cancellation
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: source predicts signing out or navigating to a public share view during generation leaves the old polling loop alive for up to five minutes, issuing requests and (after sign-out) refresh attempts. Returning and starting another run adds a separate loop; old completions still issue progress/result callbacks and success toasts. The UI cannot cancel the abandoned loop. Normal completion does stop its loop.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:43-50 loops with a new setTimeout and GET every two seconds until five minutes, done or error; there is no AbortSignal or mounted guard. Workspace's only effect at :164-174 returns no synthesis cleanup. AuthContext.jsx:31-33 can unmount Workspace on sign-out. The polling catch at Workspace.jsx:48-49 also ignores permanent 401/404.
findings.expected: R-118: polling "stops ... when ... user leaves the workspace"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "polling ends with its owner". Leaving a workspace must terminate its client polling and callbacks.
reproduction_steps: Start Synthesize on a slow job.
Sign out or navigate within the app to another routed surface before it finishes.
Return to the workspace and start another generation.
The first loop has no cleanup and keeps polling alongside the new one until its deadline/completion.

findings.title: Keyboard focus escapes modal dialogs into covered workspace actions — modal primitive supplies no focus management
findings.surface: Share, reset-link, migration and conflict modals
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts keyboard users opening Share remain focused on the background Share button and can Tab through covered Copy, Export, Save, description and project controls before reaching modal fields. They can invoke covered actions while a supposedly modal share/reset/conflict surface is open. Closing does not restore focus. Pointer users can use the modal normally; keyboard users must traverse unrelated controls and risk acting on background work.
findings.evidence: Modal.jsx:5-9 only installs Escape; :11-12 renders aria-modal dialog/backdrop, but has no focus assignment, focus trap, background inertness or restore-focus logic. ShareModal.jsx:46 uses this primitive while Workspace's editing actions remain mounted; AccountMenu.jsx:19 uses it for admin reset.
findings.expected: Checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus stays visible and follows the active surface" and "Dialog close ... restores ... focus". Modal keyboard interaction must stay on the dialog rather than reaching covered workspace controls.
reproduction_steps: Focus the workspace Share button using the keyboard and press Enter.
Press Tab repeatedly.
Focus is not moved into or contained by the Share dialog, so background controls remain in the tab order.
Close the modal with Escape; no focus restoration is performed.

findings.title: Files with non-Latin filenames cannot be downloaded — raw Unicode is placed into a latin-1 HTTP header
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts uploading a valid file named '角色设计.txt' succeeds, but downloading it raises UnicodeEncodeError while constructing the response headers because those characters cannot be encoded as latin-1. A teammate/viewer receives a failed download instead of any bytes. An uploader could rename and re-upload outside the app, but recipients cannot fix the stored name themselves.
findings.evidence: projects.py:281 preserves arbitrary original filenames; :330 removes only double quotes and :331 interpolates the name directly into the Content-Disposition header of starlette Response. requirements.txt pins starlette 0.37.2; header values use HTTP latin-1 encoding rather than Unicode filename* encoding. Files.jsx:19 needs that GET to succeed before creating a blob download.
findings.expected: R-080/R-081: downloading returns "original name and identical bytes"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: preserve "encoding ... filename". A valid Unicode filename must not prevent delivery; use an encoded filename* with a safe fallback.
reproduction_steps: Upload a small project file named 角色设计.txt.
Open Files as a member and press Download.
The download endpoint attempts to place that raw name in its response header and fails before delivering the file.

findings.title: Compare hides parameter/module/note edits and misstates old module selection — it discards those input changes and snapshots edited state
findings.surface: Compare → Input changes and Parameters & Modules
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a regeneration changing Max Health, toggling StaminaDrain and adding notes opens Compare with no corresponding Input changes chips. Its Parameters & Modules view also uses the already-toggled old module state, so a module removal can show no before/after module difference. Code/text line diff still works, but users cannot reliably audit which requested edits produced it.
findings.evidence: CompareView.jsx:34 passes params:{} and notes:"" to computeChanges and :35 removes every module change. Workspace.jsx:248-254 mutates result.modules before regeneration; :188 sets that already-edited result as previousResult. computeChanges (changes.js:27-40) only detects params/notes when supplied and needs original module state.
findings.expected: R-094: Compare "lists which inputs changed" across "parameters and modules"; request: "see the effect of dial or prompt changes"; R-086 includes parameter values, module toggles/additions and notes. Compare's previous side and changed-input list must reflect the actual previous synthesis, not edited chips.
reproduction_steps: Generate a system with a parameter and an enabled module.
Change that parameter, toggle the module off, add notes and Synthesize.
Inspect Compare's Input changes: those edits are omitted.
Switch to Parameters & Modules: the previous module is already off, hiding the actual toggle.

findings.title: Cloud projects lose their before/after comparison on reopening — only the current synthesis is persisted
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts a developer synthesizing twice, comparing and saving a cloud project loses the previous side after reload/reopen. Another Editor opening that saved project cannot inspect the changes at all. They must pay for another regeneration just to create a new pair, and the original comparison cannot be reconstructed through the app because the previous output was discarded.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:152 previousResult is only React state; :188 assigns it after an in-session run. splitResult :263-265 exports/saves result only, with no previousResult. openSystem :300 explicitly clears previousResult. backend/projects.py:127-132 stores only current system/context; :169-172 replaces them on save. CompareView.jsx:44-49 then shows 'Synthesize twice'.
findings.expected: R-095's independently checkable outcome is retrieval of previous/current sections for a cloud project; request: "Stack Systems and Compare keep working with cloud projects" and Phase 2 adds "any earlier version, not just the last one." Phase 1 should retain the immediate before/after comparison across save and reopen, without requiring full Phase 2 history or a particular API route.
reproduction_steps: Generate, tune and regenerate a system, then inspect Compare.
Save the project and reopen it (or open it on another device).
Open Compare: only the empty 'Synthesize twice' message is available.
No saved previous synthesis or changed-input record can be loaded.

findings.title: Retrying browser migration duplicates saved systems — every import mints a fresh project with no legacy identity
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts clicking Import them twice while migration is in progress or retrying its request duplicates each legacy system under fresh ids. The modal remains actionable throughout and the backend has no idempotency key. The user's cloud library becomes cluttered with duplicate projects; manual deletion is the safe recovery.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:330-334 posts every migration item to /projects/import and the Import them button at :752 has no busy guard. projects.py:152 calls create each time; :128 mints a new project_id and :133 inserts without a legacy-source identity check. server.py:42-49 has no owner/legacy-id uniqueness index.
findings.expected: R-085: posting the same browser library twice "creates no duplicate project"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Establish logical record/operation/effect identity ... retries ... concurrent creation." A given browser-saved system imported by one migration intent must create one cloud copy, while distinct legacy systems remain distinct.
reproduction_steps: Have multiple systems in the old browser library and sign in for the first time.
Click Import them twice before the first network loop finishes (or retry the same import payload).
Both loops POST the same entries.
Mine contains separately identified duplicates of each imported system.

findings.title: Failed browser migrations cannot be retried in the app — failures are swallowed and the one-time prompt is marked complete
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a transient network/storage failure during first migration leaves some or all systems unimported, then permanently suppresses the offer and labels the operation with a success toast. The raw legacy data remains in localStorage, but the new cloud-only library has no control to reopen or retry that browser library, so the user cannot recover through the intended UI without developer/storage intervention.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:334 swallows every failed per-item import; :336 emits a success toast even for zero imported; :339 writes the migration-completed key regardless of failures and :340 closes the modal. Initialization at :166-167 offers migration only if that key is absent. Browser data is not removed, but no retry UI exists.
findings.expected: R-084: "Import creates one project per browser system"; request: "Import them copies them into the account"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Walk failure boundaries for batches ... visible rejected/skipped input". Partial failures must be explained and retryable rather than marking unfinished migration complete.
reproduction_steps: Start first-sign-in Import them with legacy systems present.
Have one or more POST /projects/import requests fail (e.g. a transient network interruption).
After the loop the modal closes and reports Imported N of M.
Reload: the completion marker prevents another migration offer despite the missing projects.

findings.title: Double-clicking Save project creates duplicate cloud projects — initial save has no pending guard or operation identity
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a developer double-clicking Save project on an unsaved synthesis gets two distinct cloud projects. The UI provides no pending state and both calls show success. Manual deletion is a safe but unnecessary cleanup; this is separate from migration duplication because normal saves use a different entry point and have no migration source id.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:418 Save is disabled only when !result or readOnly, not while saving. :272-274 uses captured project state; before the first POST resolves, a second call still sees project null and POSTs again. projects.py:128/133 always mints and inserts another project, with no create operation identity.
findings.expected: Checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "pending controls and server-side operation identity preserve one create ... per intent"; request: "Save ... work as they do today, but in the cloud." Repeated clicks during a single initial Save should create one project.
reproduction_steps: Generate an unsaved system.
Click Save project twice before the first request returns.
Both captured calls choose POST /projects.
Projects → Mine contains two copies of the same initial save.

findings.title: Malformed imported project JSON crashes the workspace after being saved — importer validates only system_name
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts importing valid JSON with a system_name but tunable_parameters set to a string (or non-array modules) stores the record and then causes an uncaught frontend TypeError when ProjectsPanel opens it. The workspace becomes unusable rather than explaining the invalid file. Reload resets the open project, allowing the user to delete the broken row; ordinary valid exports do round-trip system/context correctly.
findings.evidence: projects.py:125 checks only truthy system_name; :147 accepts the whole imported dict as a system and :151-152 stores it without SystemOutput validation. Workspace.jsx:299 renders it, :362 calls tunable_parameters.forEach and :659 calls modules.map. No error boundary is present in App.js:32-40.
findings.expected: Checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "malformed/partial input ... visible rejected/skipped input"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "fields, types" must match at both ends; R-082/R-083 promise usable project import. Malformed project JSON must be refused without storing a broken project or crashing the workspace.
reproduction_steps: Use Import project with a JSON object containing system_name 'Broken' and tunable_parameters 'bad'.
The server accepts it because system_name is truthy.
The import UI immediately opens it.
Workspace's forEach/map assumptions throw instead of showing an import-validation message.

findings.title: Incomplete or unhonored generations are reported as successful — output validation checks types but not required content or edit coverage
findings.surface: Claude response → completed synthesis and Applied in this synthesis
findings.observed: AI and model features: source proves that if Claude returns a JSON object with all required keys but empty code, empty graph/setup lists, no applied_changes, or a tunable value different from an explicit override, the backend records done and the UI announces success. A user requesting Max Health=250 can receive and save a 100-valued output, with no row explaining that edit; empty output is also accepted. This is a conditional source trace of an accepted bad provider reply, not an observed model failure. Users must manually audit/retry paid generations instead of trusting the promised feedback.
findings.evidence: server.py:128 makes setup why optional with default ''; :150 defaults applied_changes to []; :143-148 accepts empty code strings and empty graph/setup lists. :303 performs only SystemOutput(**data), then :308 marks done. There is no comparison against req.change_requests, req.parameter_overrides or required output completeness. ChangePanels.jsx:36-38 hides the panel entirely when changes are absent.
findings.expected: R-087: "one applied entry per queued change"; R-089: why notes explain setup decisions; R-097: non-empty complete code/graph/setup; R-102: requested values are used. Checklist, AI and model features: "parsing, semantic validation ... empty/malformed results ... to the user-visible outcome." A structurally valid but incomplete/unapplied reply must not be confirmed as completed synthesis.
reproduction_steps: Queue a parameter change and a designer note, then Synthesize.
Consider a provider reply with the expected field types but applied_changes omitted and tunable value unchanged (or empty code/graph lists).
SystemOutput validation accepts it and marks the job done.
The UI shows success and hides the missing change report rather than rejecting/reconciling the incomplete result.

findings.title: One reset link can change the password twice concurrently — token consumption happens after an unguarded password write
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts two concurrent requests with the same reset link and different new passwords can both observe used=False and both report success, with the second password winning. The first user is then unable to sign in with the password the screen confirmed. A person retaining the same reset URL can race a legitimate redemption; another admin reset link is needed to recover safely.
findings.evidence: auth.py:229 reads a reset record; :230 checks used; :232 changes the password; only afterward :233 sets used=True using a token-only filter. There is no atomic used=False claim or transaction before the password write. ResetPassword in AuthPages.jsx:42-58 has no busy guard against overlapping submissions.
findings.expected: R-059: the reset token is "single-use" and "a second use ... is refused"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "conditional/atomic operations" must preserve effect identity under concurrent requests. Only one password change may succeed for a given token.
reproduction_steps: Obtain a fresh on-screen reset link.
Submit that token concurrently from two clients with different valid new passwords, before either marks it used.
Both requests can pass the unused check and update the password.
Only the last password works despite both submissions reporting success.

findings.title: Google-first users cannot add email/password sign-in themselves — registration rejects their email and no password-linking flow exists
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a Google-first user trying Create account with the same email is refused, and Sign in with email always fails because no password exists. They can continue using Google, but cannot add the promised second method without owner-assisted password reset, which is not an ordinary self-service linking flow.
findings.evidence: auth.py:174-178 creates Google-first users without password_hash. :128-129 rejects every registration for an existing email; :148 rejects email sign-in when password_hash is missing. No set-password/account-link action exists in AccountMenu.jsx:58-65; only an admin can issue a reset link (:214-224).
findings.expected: R-055: "Signing in with Google ... and later registering with email/password ... reaches one account"; request: "Two ways to sign in ... If both use the same email address, they reach the same account." Provide a secure authenticated way to add the password method to the existing account, without creating a duplicate.
reproduction_steps: Sign in for the first time using Google and save a project.
Sign out and choose Create account with the same email and a password.
Registration says the account already exists.
Try email Sign in: the Google-first record has no password, and there is no account control to set one.

findings.title: Older projects and files silently disappear from their lists — fixed 500-record caps have no pagination or truncation notice
findings.surface: Projects lists and Files tab at more than 500 records
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that once a user has 501 live owned projects (including repeated imports) their oldest project disappears from Mine and the count reads 500, with no way to load the remaining page. Likewise a project's 501st-oldest file is omitted from Files. Records are still stored and retrievable if an id was retained, but ordinary users cannot discover/download older work through the UI on a new device.
findings.evidence: projects.py:113/:117 use to_list(500) with no skip/cursor/total; :322 also caps file listing at 500. ProjectsPanel.jsx:71 labels lists[id].length as the count and :86 renders only those rows, with no paging/Load more action. ProjectFiles similarly renders the returned files only (:119).
findings.expected: Request: cloud Projects "saved safely and available on any device" and Files keeps project artifacts; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation" and "counts ... match the rows they summarize." All stored accessible projects/files must remain discoverable as the library grows.
reproduction_steps: Accumulate or import 501 distinct projects in one account.
Open Projects → Mine; only the newest 500 appear with count 500.
Look for the oldest project or a next-page control: neither is available.
The same cutoff applies after uploading more than 500 project files.

findings.title: Image-only PDFs are accepted but invisible to Claude — PDF processing extracts text only and sends no visual pages
findings.observed: AI and model features: source predicts a scanned spec or PDF containing a UI screenshot but no text layer uploads successfully yet supplies an empty body to Claude. No PDF bytes or rendered page images reach the model and no empty-extraction warning appears. The designer's request to match that PDF cannot be grounded in its actual content; converting it manually to an image is a safe workaround once the limitation is discovered.
findings.evidence: projects.py:261 uses only PdfReader page.extract_text() for PDF references. upload_file :294-295 calls it for any non-image reference; load_references :347-349 attaches image_bytes only when content_type starts image/. server.py:230 sends extracted PDF text, while :285 includes only image_bytes as visual content.
findings.expected: Request: "Accepted types are screenshots and images, PDFs" and "The AI uses them as source material"; R-104; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: trace "complete intended content and actual input selection". A valid PDF whose content is graphical must reach the model visually or be explicitly rejected/warned, not silently treated as empty source.
reproduction_steps: Attach a valid image-only PDF under 10 MB containing the desired UI/spec.
Ask Synthesize to follow it.
extract_text returns empty text and no image_bytes are generated for application/pdf.
The model request contains the filename but none of the PDF's visible source content.

findings.title: Notes typed while a synthesis is running disappear on completion — the old request unconditionally clears the live draft
findings.surface: Notes for next synthesis during a running generation
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a developer entering new notes for the next pass while Claude is generating loses those notes when the old request completes. They were not in that request's body, are not in result.context, and are erased from the visible field with no warning. Rewriting the short draft is the only recovery; controls suggest editing remains allowed during generation.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:187 awaits the long-running job; :189 snapshots the notes submitted at start; :190 unconditionally clears the live notes state on completion. The notes textarea at :702-710 is inside a fieldset disabled only by readOnly (:608), not loading, so users can keep editing notes while the job runs.
findings.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: input and operation state must remain coherent. R-086/request: notes before the next Synthesize must be injected rather than silently discarded.
reproduction_steps: Start a synthesis or regeneration.
While it is running, type a new note such as 'use a Gameplay Tag for stun' in Notes for next synthesis.
Wait for the current job to complete.
The new note disappears although it was never sent to that job or saved in its context.

findings.title: Reloading strands the paid synthesis result — the only job handle exists inside the old polling call
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts reloading during a generation loses the job id and returns to an idle workspace even though the server keeps generating and spending the owner's credits. The completed result remains in Mongo but is unreachable through any workspace/library action; only someone who retained the API id can retrieve it. The ordinary UI recovery is to pay for another synthesis. Normal uninterrupted polling delivers the result.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:36-38 keeps job_id only in a local async variable; no component/localStorage/project field stores it and mount at :164-174 loads only templates/migration/query project. server.py:315-318 persists jobs but only :325-330 GET-by-id retrieves them; there is no current/recent job lookup or result recovery consumer.
findings.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "interruption ... revisit ... resume ... retrieves the completed session" where supported; users rely on: "A paid background synthesis can be retrieved after an ordinary page reload rather than requiring a second paid run." R-099/R-100 describe server background generation and delivery of its finished system.
reproduction_steps: Press Synthesize and wait until the background job has started.
Reload the browser before it finishes.
The new workspace starts idle with no resume/recent-job control.
Allow the original job to finish: it is not shown or recoverable in Projects unless the original page had saved its result.

findings.title: Oversized uploads can exhaust worker memory before rejection — file limits are checked only after an unbounded read
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: source predicts a signed-in user's oversized 1 GB upload is fully read into a bytes object before its eventual 413, and concurrent such uploads multiply the allocation. The documented 25 MB ceiling therefore does not bound worker memory, risking interruptions to other users' saves/generations under a reachable large-upload workload. No runtime memory/latency measurement was made; exact failure depends on deployment memory.
findings.evidence: projects.py:284 executes data = await file.read() without a size bound, then :285-287 applies 10/25 MB limits using len(data). The multipart UploadFile may be disk-spooled, but this call materializes the entire uploaded body in application memory before rejection.
findings.expected: Request: "10 MB per reference file and 25 MB per project file"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "buffering ... bounds and backpressure" must prevent material resource growth for reachable input. Oversized uploads must be rejected without unbounded application-memory buffering.
reproduction_steps: As a member with Editor access, upload a project file much larger than 25 MB.
The endpoint reads the full file into memory first.
Only after that allocation does it return the size-limit error.
Concurrent oversized uploads repeat that full allocation per request.

findings.title: Admin reset-link creation stops working after access-token expiry — refresh interceptor skips protected auth routes
findings.surface: Account menu → Password reset link → Create
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts an email-signed-in admin waiting over 15 minutes then choosing Password reset link receives 'Not authenticated' on Create, repeatedly, despite the still-valid refresh session. Other project API calls refresh automatically, but this action never does. Reloading or forcing an unrelated project request restores it; this is bounded but confusing account-management failure.
findings.evidence: api.js:11 excludes every URL beginning /auth/ from refresh/retry. AccountMenu.jsx:14 posts /auth/admin/reset-link, whose backend Depends(admin_user) calls current_user and returns 401 after the 15-minute access expiry (auth.py:16,86-96). The refresh cookie remains valid seven days (:17,42).
findings.expected: Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Trace token storage ... expiry ... refresh/retry where refresh tokens exist"; R-058: admin can create an on-screen reset link. An active admin with a valid refresh session must not need unrelated navigation or reload for this protected account action.
reproduction_steps: Sign in as admin using email/password.
Wait beyond the 15-minute access-token lifetime without making a refreshing API call.
Open Account menu → Password reset link and press Create for a valid user.
The /auth/ exclusion prevents refresh, so Create fails until reload or another non-auth API call renews access.

findings.title: Viewer project regeneration is restricted only in the UI — generation requests have no enforced project identity or Editor check
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a Viewer sending a project regeneration directly can start a paid Claude job and obtain its revised output because project identity is ignored, whereas the UI says regeneration requires Editor access. Saving back to the shared project is correctly refused, so this is a bounded generation-role violation rather than unauthorized durable project mutation. The endpoint must distinguish an allowed new personal synthesis from a regeneration of an existing role-restricted project.
findings.evidence: server.py:77 configures extra='ignore'; GenerateRequest :79-95 has no project_id and generate_system :312 requires only current_user, not load_project(..., 'editor'). Workspace.jsx:213-221 sends a previous system without project identity; only the frontend readOnly flag at :161 and fieldsets prevent Viewer synthesis. In contrast projects.py:163 and :279-280 do check editor access for saves/uploads.
findings.expected: R-073: "a generate request attributed to that project [from a Viewer is] refused ... while ... Editor ... succeed"; request: "Viewer: can open, copy, export and download only"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: reject "client-only checks without server enforcement." Project regeneration must enforce the current project's role server-side.
reproduction_steps: Open a project shared as Viewer and note that Synthesize is disabled.
Using an authorized API client, submit its regeneration request with that project's identity and previous output.
GenerateRequest ignores the project identity and starts a job for the Viewer.
The same request is never checked against the member's current Viewer role.

findings.title: Accepted long passwords ignore their suffix, so an old password can survive reset — bcrypt's 72-byte limit conflicts with the 128-character input contract
findings.surface: Email registration, sign-in and password reset with long/Unicode passwords
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts two accepted passwords sharing the first 72 UTF-8 bytes but differing later authenticate as the same password. A user resetting an 80-character passphrase by changing its tail can still sign in with the old password, and Unicode passwords reach this byte boundary with fewer than 72 characters. The remaining prefix still supplies entropy, so the evidence supports a bounded password-identity failure rather than a general bypass. Users are not told to change the earlier prefix to recover.
findings.evidence: auth.py:102/:113 accepts passwords up to 128 characters, :24 hashes password.encode() directly and :28 verifies the same way. backend/requirements.txt:9 pins bcrypt==4.1.3, whose bcrypt input semantics use only the first 72 bytes. There is no byte-length validator or full-length prehash.
findings.expected: Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "password hashing" and valid/wrong-password handling must preserve the supported password's identity; users rely on: "All characters of an accepted password determine whether it authenticates." For a reset, changing a supported password must invalidate the old distinct password, not ignore its suffix.
reproduction_steps: Register using a valid password longer than 72 UTF-8 bytes but within the 128-character limit.
Through a fresh reset link choose a different password with the same first 72 bytes and a changed suffix.
Sign out and try the old password.
bcrypt 4.1.3 ignores the differing suffix and accepts the old password too.

findings.title: Retrying a lost synthesis response spends credits twice — generation creation has no stable operation identity
findings.surface: Synthesize → ambiguous initial network failure → retry
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that if the server creates a job but its initial POST response is lost, the UI immediately reports failure and allows Retry/Synthesize. Retrying creates a second independent Claude call while the first continues spending credits; the first result is unreachable through the UI. Any signed-in developer on an unreliable connection can unintentionally charge the owner twice for one requested synthesis. The issue is retry identity, distinct from duplicate cloud Save records.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:38-40 treats a failed POST response as a failed generation without reconciling a possible job already started. server.py:314-319 creates a fresh random job id and task on every POST, with no caller-supplied operation key/unique intent lookup. The client retains no pending operation handle before the POST response.
findings.expected: Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "retries ... preserve the operation's identity" and "a send timing out after delivery must reconcile before retrying"; request: "Every AI generation ... is paid from the app owner's ... balance." One synthesis intent must not incur two generations solely because its accepted response was lost.
reproduction_steps: Start Synthesize.
Have the initial POST response fail after the backend has inserted the job and started its task.
After the visible Generation failed message, press Synthesize again.
The backend starts a second job rather than returning/recovering the first operation.

findings.title: Reopened systems regenerate from an unrelated description — the library saves output but not its generation context
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a developer who saves an inventory system, reloads the page, opens it and adjusts a parameter sends the initial melee-combat prompt (:164), ActorComponent and default architecture settings to the model. The saved inventory parameters are mixed into that combat request. Similarly, opening a different saved system retains the preceding system's prompt/settings. The output can be viewed correctly, but continuing customization of saved work requires manually reconstructing the description and settings; they are not recoverable from the saved record. The wrong request is source-proven; the model's resulting content is not observed.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:241 stores only `{ ...result, saved_at: ... }`; :244-247 loadFromLibrary only calls setResult(item) and setTab("graph"); :200-210 generates from current prompt, bpClass, dials, replicated and extra rather than the saved system. backend/server.py:61-74 SystemOutput has no original prompt or generation settings.
findings.expected: request: "Save/manage generated systems in a personal library" selected through "All of the above", and "outputs were tunable via sliders ... alterations/customizations"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "revisit reaches valid work for the same operation." Loading a saved system for further tuning must restore that system's original generation context rather than silently use another system's prompt.
reproduction_steps: Choose Grid Inventory, change its architecture dials or NET setting, synthesize, and Save.
Reload the page.
Open the saved inventory entry in My Library.
Adjust one System Parameter and press Synthesize System.
The submitted prompt is the default melee-combat prompt and the saved generation settings have not been restored.

findings.title: C++ code displays corrupted markup instead of clean highlighted code — regex passes rewrite their own HTML tags
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: any generated C++ containing a comment or string triggers overlapping substitutions. For example, the quotes in the tok-com class attribute are themselves replaced with a tok-str span, and subsequent keyword replacement rewrites the literal class attribute names. Thus the highlighter returns malformed nested markup which the browser must repair, exposing markup fragments and corrupting the code's visual rendering. Developers cannot reliably read the C++ in the viewer, although Copy/download still use the original code and provide a recovery path. This conclusion comes from tracing the string transformations, not a browser observation.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/highlight.js:20 wraps comments in `<span class="tok-com">`; :22 applies its string regex to the entire resulting HTML, including the new class attribute; :27-28 applies CPP_KEYWORDS, which contains "class" (:3), to the whole HTML again. frontend/src/App.js:102,127 inserts that string with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
findings.expected: request: "All of the above" includes readable C++ snippets; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Compare complete intended content ... with delivered output." Highlighting must preserve the exact visible code and only decorate tokens, not tokenize the HTML it just generated.
reproduction_steps: Synthesize a system whose C++ contains a normal // comment and a quoted include filename.
Open C++ Snippets.
The highlighter wraps the comment, then matches quotes and the word class inside its generated tags, producing malformed viewer HTML.

findings.title: Excluding a custom module sends contradictory instructions — the module remains in both include and remove lists
findings.surface: Modules → add module → generated module chip → Synthesize System; POST /api/generate
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: add StaminaDrain, synthesize an output containing it, toggle its generated chip off, and synthesize again. StaminaDrain is still in extra and is also in removed, so the backend explicitly instructs the model both to include and exclude the same logical module. The requested exclusion is not represented as a single authoritative decision, making the advertised add/subtract flow unreliable and requiring the user to discover and remove the separate extra chip as well. The contradictory request is source-proven; which instruction the model follows is not observed.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:235 adds the name to extra; :225-230 toggles only result.modules[].included, never extra; :198 builds removed from false modules and :208-209 sends extra_modules: extra and removed_modules: removed. backend/server.py:140-141 labels the same lists "User-added modules to INCLUDE" and "User-removed modules to mark excluded"; :100 asks for included:true and included:false respectively.
findings.expected: request: "some type of add/subtract options to integrate/expand upon"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "repeated toggles preserve the chosen state." A module toggled off must be unambiguously excluded on the next synthesis, not simultaneously demanded as included.
reproduction_steps: Add StaminaDrain in Modules and synthesize.
Toggle the generated StaminaDrain chip from included to excluded.
Leave the separate added-module chip in place and press Synthesize System.
The request includes StaminaDrain in both extra_modules and removed_modules.

findings.title: A malformed model parameter can blank the workspace — nested output records are accepted without the types the UI requires
findings.observed: AI and model features: a provider result containing an otherwise valid SystemOutput with a parameter such as {key:'max_health', label:{text:'Max Health'}, value:100} passes the backend's List[dict] validation. The result is announced as generated and set into React state; rendering the object as Slider's label throws React's invalid-child error, unmounting the workspace rather than producing the intended retryable generation failure. The same weakness affects module and setup text fields. This is a conditional source-backed failure for malformed provider JSON, not a claim that Claude emitted it during this review. Reload can recover previously saved systems, but the just-generated work is lost.
findings.evidence: backend/server.py:65 declares tunable_parameters: List[dict], :66 modules: List[dict], :70 setup_guide: List[dict]; :183 validates SystemOutput and :188 sends it as result. frontend/src/App.js:502 passes p.label directly to Slider; :65 renders {label}, and :66 renders {value}. frontend/src/index.js:17-23 mounts App without an error boundary.
findings.expected: checklist, AI and model features: "Follow parsing, semantic validation ... against the ... field/format ... contract" and "Trace empty/malformed results ... to the user-visible outcome." The backend should enforce the nested shapes required by its consumers and show a recoverable generation error for invalid output rather than accept a result that crashes the app.
reproduction_steps: Synthesize a system.
Consider the reachable provider-response condition that one tunable parameter's label is an object rather than a string while all top-level fields are present.
The backend accepts this dictionary and emits a result event.
The System Parameters render attempts to place the object in a span and the app has no error boundary.

findings.title: Narrow-screen users cannot read generated output — fixed sidebars consume more than the entire viewport
findings.surface: Workspace on narrow screens; all center output tabs
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: at 375px the two nonshrinking sidebars require 320+340=660px before any output space is allocated. The main has min-width:0 and consequently collapses to zero width; its Event Graph clips all nodes and its other output views have no usable reading width. Hiding tab text below lg does not free the sidebar allocation. Developers using narrow screens can generate but cannot use the central viewers normally; an export/another device may recover the text, so this is graded as a bounded presentation/interaction impairment. This is a source-based layout prediction, not a browser measurement.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:303 uses a single horizontal flex row; :306 fixes the left aside to w-[320px] shrink-0; :476 fixes the right aside to w-[340px] shrink-0, with no responsive variants; :382 main is flex-1 min-w-0. NodeGraph.jsx:67 clips overflow in its w-full canvas. The only responsive changes to tabs (:404) and chips (:293) hide labels, not the panels.
findings.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "Check containment ... and reachable controls under supported viewports" and "primary content ... without ... clipping." Users rely on: "the web app lets them read generated output on a narrow screen, not just submit the description." At 375px the panels should reflow/collapse or provide a usable output pane.
reproduction_steps: Open the app with a 375px-wide viewport.
Synthesize a system.
Try Event Graph, C++ Snippets and Setup Guide.
Both fixed-width sidebars remain in the row, leaving the center output pane no allocated width.

findings.title: Save reports success and can crash when storage is full — persistence errors are uncaught and occur after confirmation
findings.surface: Save / My Library; useLibrary persistence effect
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: when the saved collection exceeds the browser's storage quota (or storage writes are denied), Save first reports success and then the effect throws. Persistence has not happened and the unhandled effect error can unmount the workspace; reloading restores only the previous collection, losing the allegedly saved generation. No limit, eviction, write error handling or in-memory recovery is implemented. This is a conditional source prediction, not a storage-quota test. It affects developers accumulating systems or running under storage restrictions; they can recover older saves on reload, but not trust the new-save confirmation.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:55 catches read/parse failures but :57 calls localStorage.setItem(LS_KEY, JSON.stringify(items)) in an effect with no try/catch. :241 updates React state and :242 immediately reports "Saved to library", before that effect persists the new collection. frontend/src/index.js:17-23 has no error boundary.
findings.expected: request: "Save/manage generated systems in a personal library" selected through "All of the above"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "A failed save ... [must not be] presented as confirmed"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "caches/queues have effective bounds or eviction." A full or unavailable local store must show a recoverable save failure and preserve the current generated system.
reproduction_steps: Use My Library until a further full-collection write would exceed the browser's local-storage quota, or use a browser context denying storage writes.
Synthesize another system and press Save.
The app reports Saved to library before attempting the uncaught write.
Reload: the newly confirmed save is not in the durable library.

findings.title: Saving in a second tab deletes the first tab's saved work — each tab overwrites storage from a stale library snapshot
findings.surface: My Library / Save in two browser tabs
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: open two tabs with the same initial library. Tab A saves system A, then tab B saves distinct system B. B merges against its stale React array and overwrites localStorage without A. Reloading either tab now permanently loses A from My Library, despite A having received a successful save confirmation. There is no server copy or import path to restore it. The overwritten record may still be visible in tab A until it is closed/reloaded, allowing a temporary manual re-save, but ordinary multiple-tab use silently loses valid saved work.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:54-55 reads the library only in the useState initializer; :57 overwrites the entire stored array on each local change; :241 merges a save only into that tab's lib snapshot. No storage listener or later storage read exists in App.js to reconcile another tab's updates.
findings.expected: checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Walk plausible interleavings ... Check ... lost/overwritten valid work ... using actors the app can actually run concurrently." Users rely on: "saving a different system in a second browser tab does not delete previously saved systems." Independently generated systems have distinct backend UUIDs (backend/server.py:181) and must coexist.
reproduction_steps: Open the app in two tabs before saving either new system.
In tab A synthesize and Save system A.
In tab B synthesize and Save a different system B.
Reload tab A: system A is gone from My Library.

findings.title: Long descriptions fail without telling developers what to fix — the UI omits the API limit and discards field-validation errors
findings.surface: AI Synthesizer prompt → Synthesize System; 422 error rendering
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: entering a detailed 2001-character system description is allowed by the UI, but FastAPI rejects it with an array-valued validation detail. streamGenerate discards the field and rule and displays only Request failed (422). No character limit/count is exposed, so the developer cannot tell whether the description, sliders or another setting caused the refusal and must guess what to edit. Shortening the prompt can recover the main task; the defect is opaque, mismatched validation, not an API failure to enforce its limit.
findings.evidence: backend/server.py:32 enforces prompt max_length=2000. frontend/src/App.js:313-320 renders a textarea with no maxLength or length message; :191 checks only a lower bound; :30-31 discards non-string j.detail and substitutes `Request failed (${res.status})`. FastAPI's supplied HTTPValidationError schema defines detail as an array of loc/msg/type records (openapi.json, components.schemas.HTTPValidationError).
findings.expected: checklist, Business logic and calculations: "Error messages identify the violated rule beside its field"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Compare request/response contracts at both ends ... error keys." A developer whose description exceeds the API's 2000-character contract should see the prompt limit and know how to correct it, rather than a generic status code.
reproduction_steps: Enter a system description of 2001 characters in AI Synthesizer.
Press Synthesize System.
Observe the source-predicted Synthesis Failed message Request failed (422), without the prompt's 2000-character limit.

findings.title: Touch and keyboard users cannot reach offscreen graph nodes — panning is mouse-only and zoom cannot fit the graph
findings.surface: Event Graph pan/drag on touch or keyboard input
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: on a 1024px-wide touch-only viewport, at most 1024-660=364px remains for the graph. A valid rightmost node at x=1200 extends to (1200+190)*0.4=556px even at minimum zoom. The canvas is overflow-hidden, has no scroll/pan alternative, and responds only to mouse dragging; tapping its zoom buttons cannot expose that final node. Keyboard-only users face the same lack of a pan action. The graph cannot be fully inspected under these supported browser input conditions, although textual outputs remain alternatives. This is a source-based reachability calculation, not a touch-device test.
findings.evidence: NodeGraph.jsx:69-72 installs only onMouseDown/onMouseMove/onMouseUp/onMouseLeave; :114 node dragging also uses onMouseDown. The controls are keyboard-focusable, but operation by value/position guesswork is not equivalent to named controls. findings_minor.title: Single-system stack requests spend credits instead of being rejected — backend stack validation has no lower bound

A stack request with one source must be rejected before spending generation credits (empty stack_systems must remain valid for ordinary non-stack synthesis).
reproduction_steps: Submit POST /api/generate with a valid prompt and stack_systems containing one saved system.
The request passes Pydantic validation.
A background generation starts and is instructed to merge a single system instead of refusing the invalid stack.

findings_minor.title: Fit can leave dragged nodes offscreen — its minimum zoom prevents framing a widely spread graph
findings_minor.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts after panning/dragging a node far from the rest, Fit still clips distant nodes because its 30% floor prevents scaling them into the canvas. The numeric witness is a source geometry calculation, not a measured viewport render.
findings_minor.evidence: NodeGraph.jsx:29-31 computes graph bounds then clamps the fit zoom to at least 0.3. :33 aligns its minimum corner rather than adding any alternate overview. :51-53 permits dragging nodes arbitrarily far apart. Press Fit.

Use pan or Reset to recover visibility.

Switch to C++ Snippets, then back to Setup Guide.

findings_minor.title: New systems inherit another graph's dragged node positions — view state is keyed only by reusable local node IDs

findings_minor.title: Copy failures leave developers without feedback — clipboard permission errors are unhandled
findings_minor.surface: Blueprint Pseudocode and C++ Snippets → Copy

findings_minor.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:103-106 defines an async copy handler that awaits navigator.clipboard.writeText(code || "") and only handles success; :123 passes it directly to onClick. There is no catch or fallback for a rejected write, or guard for an unavailable clipboard API.

reproduction_steps: Use a secure browser context whose policy or permission denies clipboard writes.
Generate a system and open Blueprint Pseudocode or C++ Snippets.
Press Copy.

findings_minor.title: An earlier synthesis overrides a later library selection — completion does not check whether its result is still selected

findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: while synthesis is pending, a developer can click a saved item and receive Loaded: <saved name>. Its display is still covered by the synthesis overlay, and when the earlier request completes, setResult(data) replaces that later selection with the newly generated system. The saved system is not deleted and can be opened again after completion, so this is a minor but real lost-selection/status inconsistency. The timing and unconditional overwrite are source-proven; this was not exercised at runtime.
findings_minor.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:200 awaits streamGenerate and :212 unconditionally calls setResult(data). :244-247 loads a saved item with setResult(item), but does not abort/invalidate the active request. :370-371 keeps library load buttons enabled during loading; :414 places the loading overlay only inside the center pane.
findings_minor.expected: checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions" and "a delayed completion callback [must not] change a newly started session." Users rely on: "opening a saved system remains the selected system unless they choose another result." A later library selection should cancel/supersede the pending display update, or loading a different system should be clearly unavailable until it completes.
reproduction_steps: Have at least one saved system in My Library.
Start synthesizing a different description.
Before it finishes, click the saved system's library entry.
The app announces it loaded, but the earlier generation's completion replaces it.
